{"subject":"Tail latency on self-managed Cassandra","body":"Hi Lior,

Thanks for connecting. I caught your talk on running 60 self-managed Apache Cassandra nodes for the Kestrel Games leaderboard cluster, especially the part on tail latency and GC/compaction tuning.

That GC angle is where ScyllaDB tends to come up: its shard-per-core C++ architecture has no JVM garbage-collection pauses, which keeps p99 latency predictable without the same tuning effort.

If it's useful, I'd be glad to share how other teams have compared p99 behavior on similar leaderboard workloads. Would that be worth a look?

Best,
Oz
GTM Engineer, ScyllaDB
